memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the Lord said to him, "Not so; anyone who kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over." Then the Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him. - Gen 4:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is grace where we least expect it. Cain is a murderer, unrepentant and full of self-pity - and God protects him. The mark on Cain is not a brand of shame but a shield of mercy, a promise that God will restrain violence against him. The very One Cain sinned against becomes his protector.

This tells us something staggering about God's heart. His mercy reaches even the undeserving. He does not deal with us as our sins deserve (Ps 103:10). Even when He judges, He tempers judgement with kindness, giving space for life to continue.

We should be careful not to see this as God approving of Cain. It is not approval; it is patience - the same patience that gives every one of us breath and time we have not earned. God's kindness is meant to lead us to repentance (Rom 2:4).

If God showed such mercy to Cain, how much more has He shown to us in Christ, who died not for the righteous but for the ungodly (Rom 5:8)? The mark of protection on Cain points to a greater mark - the seal of God's Spirit on all who belong to Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you underestimated how merciful God is?
- Is God's patience leading you toward repentance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Merciful Father, thank You that You do not treat me as my sins deserve. Let Your kindness lead me deeper into repentance and trust.
